entry.evidence: the current study aims to identify the processes regulating groundwater chemistry to overcome related problems in Asyut region

sequences.source_document: Publisher XML full text (jats_text), with published PDF for figures

steps.action: The authors pose the aim of identifying the natural and anthropogenic processes that control groundwater chemistry in the Asyut Quaternary aquifer, framed as a management need.
steps.quote: the current study aims to identify the processes regulating groundwater chemistry to overcome related problems in Asyut region

steps.action: Candidate anthropogenic sources (sewage leakage, latrines, intensive fertilization) are taken from Egyptian literature as expected influences on groundwater quality.
steps.quote: Groundwater pollution due to the absence/deterioration of sewage systems and intensive fertilization has received attention in Egyptian literature

steps.action: The aquifer's stratigraphy, confinement (confined floodplain, unconfined desert fringe), climate and recharge sources are summarized from earlier studies.
steps.quote: Geology and hydrogeology of the aquifer have been discussed in the literature

steps.action: The analysis is designed around PCA plus Gibbs, end-member, Visual MINTEQ saturation-index and Piper diagrams. The authors acknowledge that PCA gives links between variables rather than cause and effect.
steps.quote: Multivariate statistics were applied to identify the relationship between groundwater variables and their origin.

steps.action: Thirty-four pumping wells were sampled. T, pH, TDS, EC and Eh were measured in situ; major ions were measured by spectrophotometry and titration, and Fe and Mn by ICP-MS.
steps.quote: Thirty-four groundwater samples were taken from pumping wells in Asyut Governorate, Egypt

steps.action: The field electrode was calibrated before readings, and ionic charge balances were computed to check the analytical accuracy; all errors were below 5%.
steps.quote: Charge balances were calculated to verify the accuracy of chemical analyses; the error was less than 5% for all samples analyzed

steps.action: COD values for the same wells are taken from the authors' own earlier study (Abd-Elgawad et al. 2021).
steps.quote: COD values build upon a previous work by Abd-Elgawad et al. (1) for the same wells.

steps.action: KMO (0.7) and Bartlett's sphericity tests are run to check that the data set is adequate for PCA against conventional thresholds.
steps.quote: In this study, KMO = 0.7, above the minimum requirement of 0.5, with Bartlett’s test for sphericity of 0.00

steps.action: PCA decision rules are fixed: varimax rotation, retention of components with eigenvalue > 1, and interpretation of loadings ≥ 0.5 as a baseline.
steps.quote: Furthermore, PCs that had an eigenvalue > 1 were kept, and the rest was removed.

steps.action: Descriptive statistics (CV%, percentiles, IQR, box plots) are compared with WHO and FAO guidelines. The dispersion of TDS, Na, SO4 and Cl is read as evidence of mixed natural and anthropogenic control.
steps.quote: Descriptive statistics of physio-chemical data are presented in Table 1 and Fig. 3, in comparison to WHO (27) and FAO (6) guidelines.

steps.action: Outlier wells for TDS, Cl and NO3 are located on the unconfined desert fringe, which establishes a spatial salinity and nitrate pattern.
steps.quote: The samples displaying anomalous TDS values (outliers) are located close to the border of highly mineralized desert fringe under unconfined conditions

steps.action: Anomalous Fe in residential wells is attributed to iron pipe corrosion, supported by organic pollution in shallow wells.
steps.quote: The anomalous Fe values (Fig. 3) in the residential communities refer to iron pipe corrosion.

steps.action: Piper classification separates bicarbonate floodplain waters (group A) from chloride/sulfate desert-fringe waters (group B), read as a lateral mineralization path (Fig. 4, p. 8).
steps.quote: water types changed laterally from low mineralized floodplain aquifer to highly mineralized unconfined desert aquifer

steps.action: Samples are placed on Gibbs (Fig. 5, p. 8) and Gaillardet end-member (Fig. 6, p. 9) diagrams. They fall in the rock-dominance field, with evaporation and ion-exchange signals, between the silicate and evaporite end-members.
steps.quote: Samples fall under rock dominance area implying that the rock-water interaction is the most dominant process controlling groundwater chemistry.

steps.action: Regional mineralogy from Omer (1996) is cited to support silicate weathering as the source of Na, K, Ca and Mg.
steps.quote: Regional geology (Omer, 14) favors silicate weathering as a potential source of these cations

steps.action: The authors propose that nitric and sulfuric acid from agrochemicals drive silicate weathering, and write the general reactions.
steps.quote: Multivariate statistics explained the role of nitrogen- and sulfur-bearing materials (agrochemicals) in silicate weathering.

steps.action: Saturation indices computed with Visual MINTEQ 3.1 show halite, gypsum and anhydrite undersaturated in all samples, offered as confirmation of evaporite dissolution.
steps.quote: Dissolution of evaporite minerals was confirmed using V. MINTEQ 3.1, where halite, gypsum, and anhydrite are undersaturated in all sampled water

steps.action: Varimax-rotated PCA on 15 variables extracts three components explaining 74% of the variance (Table 2).
steps.quote: Three rotated components representing 74% of the dataset explain the processes controlling groundwater chemistry (Table 2; Fig. 7).

steps.action: PC1 (TDS, major ions and NO3, inverse with pH) is interpreted as a mixed factor: natural weathering enhanced by acidification from N fertilizer.
steps.quote: PC1 can be considered as a mixed factor explaining the natural weathering due to acidification under N fertilizer application.

steps.action: The PC1 interpretation is cross-checked against the Piper (recharge from irrigation return flow and sewage) and Gibbs/end-member (silicate and evaporite weathering) results from the same data.
steps.quote: Gibbs and end-member diagrams (Figs. 5 and 6) suggest that the chemistry of major ions is regulated by silicate and evaporite weathering.

steps.action: A rival explanation for Fe and Mn is cited: Omer (2003) attributed them to sediment texture and to heavy minerals of the Ghawanim formation.
steps.quote: who found that Fe and Mn content increases upwards towards the finer sediments and Ghawanim formation rich in heavy minerals

steps.action: The negative loading of Fe and Mn against Eh on PC2 is read as redox control. The compositional/textural rival is rejected, and PC2 is named a redox factor.
steps.quote: Fe and Mn contents are controlled by the redox process and not by compositional/textural features as discussed [...] )

steps.action: PC3 (COD and HCO3 inverse with depth) is interpreted as organic pollution concentrated in shallow wells, whose oxidation produces bicarbonate. This is cross-referenced to the inferred sewage pipe corrosion.
steps.quote: PC3 is responsible for 12.7% of the variance, showing COD and HCO3− negatively correlated with depth

steps.action: The conclusion is retained: mixed natural and anthropogenic control (agriculture, organic pollution), N fertilizer enhancing weathering, redox control of Fe and Mn, and a lateral facies change; management recommendations follow.
steps.quote: Groundwater is influenced by anthropogenic contributions viz agricultural activities and organic pollution.

tree.answer: Wide spatial variation in groundwater quality across the Asyut aquifer
No; the controlling processes are inferred from ion chemistry
Identify the processes that control groundwater chemistry
Natural (weathering, evaporation, ion exchange) vs anthropogenic (fertilizer, sewage); for Fe and Mn, redox vs sediment texture
Not stated in advance; PCA loadings and diagrams are interpreted after the fact
Conditions found: one field sampling of 34 wells; nothing set
Only premise checks (charge balance, KMO) and agreement among diagrams on the same data; no robustness tests
Mixed natural and anthropogenic control and redox control of Fe and Mn retained as the best explanation

end.claim: Groundwater chemistry in the Asyut Quaternary aquifer is controlled by natural weathering (silicate and evaporite) and evaporation together with anthropogenic inputs (N fertilizer enhancing weathering, organic sewage pollution), and Fe and Mn are controlled by redox.

decisive_move.sentence: The varimax PCA that extracts three components (mixed weathering/fertilizer, redox, shallow organic pollution) is the step without which the headline attributions would not exist.

gates.evidence: Sampling served a general aim rather than a stated hypothesis (§1 ¶1, §2.1 ¶1). The only test the claim faced is the PC2 reading against Omer's textural rival, and that rival was not tested with a texture or lithology variable (§3.4 ¶2). Gibbs and end-member placement could in principle have failed (§3.3 ¶1). PCA thresholds (KMO > 0.5, eigenvalue > 1, loading ≥ 0.5) are conventional rules described as fixed 'to deal impartially', but the paper does not say whether they were set before the data were seen (§2.2 ¶1).

imports.item: Principal component analysis with varimax rotation (Kaiser 1960)
Kaiser–Meyer–Olkin and Bartlett sphericity adequacy tests (Tabachnick & Fidell 2007); SPSS 16.0
Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry for Fe and Mn
WHO (2017) drinking-water guideline values used as reference thresholds
FAO (1994) water quality for agriculture guideline ranges

limits: No peer-review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded. The sampling date and season are not given; the data are a single campaign of 34 wells, available only on request. No field replicates, blanks or reference materials are reported; QA is limited to electrode calibration and charge balance. The filtration size '45 µm' is probably 0.45 µm (inference). Table 1 and Fig. 3 give Fe and Mn in µg/L while the text uses mg/l. PCA uses n=34 for 15 variables. The Piper group A/B membership of individual wells is not listed. Reasoning about pipe corrosion and organic pollution is circular: §3.1 ¶1 uses organic pollution to confirm pipe corrosion, and §3.4 ¶2 uses pipe corrosion to confirm organic pollution. MINTEQ undersaturation shows that evaporites could dissolve, not that they do (inference). The exclusion of Omer's textural explanation rests on a PC2 correlation without any texture variable, and Omer studied a different area. Sub-claims and their statuses: Fe from pipe corrosion is a hypothesis without test ('most probably' in §0 ¶1), status none. 'N fertilization impact on natural weathering has been demonstrated' (§0 ¶1) rests on NO3 loading on PC1, status best_explanation at most. Redox control of Fe and Mn is best_explanation. The lateral facies change (Piper) is a described pattern within one data set, not tested as regularity_in_range. Composition is none_fits because the walk is a single-campaign descriptive and multivariate interpretation: no crucial test among rivals, no repetition over independent traces, and no fitted regularity across repeated cases.

disagreements.target: Omer (2003), Fe and Mn controlled by sediment texture and heavy-mineral-rich Ghawanim formation
disagreements.support: The negative loading of Fe and Mn against Eh on PC2 is taken to show redox rather than compositional/textural control, without a texture variable in the analysis.
disagreements.quote: Fe and Mn contents are controlled by the redox process and not by compositional/textural features as discussed [...] )

alternatives_considered.reason: the most widely used method in the literature

alternatives_considered.chosen: Redox control of Fe and Mn
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Compositional/textural control (finer sediments, heavy-mineral-rich Ghawanim formation; Omer 2003)
alternatives_considered.reason: Fe and Mn load negatively with Eh on PC2

alternatives_considered.chosen: Mixed natural and anthropogenic origin of PC1
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Purely anthropogenic origin (NO3 marker, Piper recharge) or purely natural origin (normal concentrations, Gibbs/end-member weathering)
alternatives_considered.reason: NO3 loading on PC1 indicates anthropogenic input, while normal concentrations and weathering diagrams indicate natural origin
